tldr: Canadian signals are thin but meaningful: Wealthsimple is opening betas for a CAD cash product with 3.25% promo rewards and for a Canadian-dollar stablecoin, and CIBC is adding a U.S. CDR. Elsewhere, stablecoins, AI-driven payments and 24/7 trading are setting new customer expectations, while Nubank's Brazil banking license and U.S. launch show a fintech moving toward full-bank status.
themes: Stablecoins and tokenized money going mainstream
Fintechs becoming full banks and expanding cross-border
Promo-led acquisition (rewards, card bonuses, Buen Fin)

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple opens a CADD beta with 3.25% promotional rewards and a retail beta for Tetra's Canadian-dollar stablecoin
highlights.why: Our most direct digital rival is pairing a promo-rate cash product with CAD stablecoin access, which raises expectations for rates and for crypto-adjacent features among self-directed Canadians.

highlights.headline: CIBC to launch an additional U.S. Canadian Depositary Receipt
highlights.why: A direct competitor (and our parent's peer set) is widening cross-border equity access through CDRs, which could set a benchmark for Canadian investors who want U.S. stock exposure without currency conversion.

highlights.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so AI agents can pay on users' behalf without seeing card details, and Starling ships an AI 'talk to transact' feature
highlights.why: Agentic and voice-driven payments are moving from concept to product, so we should consider how our cards and app will work with AI agents and conversational payment flows.

highlights.headline: SoFi takes SoFiUSD, a bank-issued stablecoin and the first tokenized deposit product at a US bank, live on Polygon, its third blockchain, reaching 17M members
highlights.why: A bank-licensed player is treating tokenized deposits as a core product, a category shift that could eventually pressure Canadian banks to offer similar rails.
